title: Identity and Security Boundaries
readerIntent: Understand who may access each Nodics surface and why credential flows remain separate.
owner: Profile owns persisted identities; nAuth owns reusable credential security; every target module owns authorization
summary: Axis employees, consumer customers, and internal modules or scheduled processes are three distinct security boundaries with different credentials, audiences, permissions, and lifecycle rules.

sections.heading: Three non-interchangeable boundaries
items: Employee: human login and access token for permitted BackOffice operations; Axis is never for customer accounts.
Customer: human login and ownership-scoped access to consumer application capabilities.
Module or scheduled process: service principal, API key, and bounded internal service token; never a person's username/password or bearer session.

sections.heading: Independent gates
items: Authentication proves the caller identity and credential validity.
Authorization decides whether that principal may perform the target action.
Tenant and ownership policy constrain which records and fields are reachable.
API exposure decides whether a sensitive route family exists in the topology.
Business validation still governs the requested transition.
